tip: 'Gaan' + infinitive marks a planned future: 'zij gaat lopen' (she is going to run), signalling intention rather than a neutral prediction.
'Zou' plus 'moeten' plus infinitive gives advice, like 'should': 'hij zou meer moeten sporten' (he should exercise more).
'Zou willen dat' takes the past tense for a present wish: 'zij zou willen dat zij tijd had' (she wishes she had time).
Fronting 'nauwelijks' (hardly) forces the verb before the subject: 'nauwelijks was hij vertrokken', not 'nauwelijks hij was'.
'Zowel ... als ...' means both ... and: 'zowel de leraar als de leerlingen' (both the teacher and the pupils).
'Hetzij ... hetzij ...' means either ... or: 'hetzij door studie, hetzij door ervaring' (whether by study or by experience).
'Ook al' means even though and is followed by inversion: 'ook al was iedereen moe' (even though everyone was tired).
